newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares fall in their first week on BSE.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares fall in their first week on BSE.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed in their first week of trade on the Beirut Stock exchange (BSE) ended on Friday.
A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the central Beirut disctrict SOLIDERE is rebuilding, fell to $111.25 from last Friday's $112.5.
B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, rose to $115 from $113 last Friday -- the last day of trade for both shares on the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market.
The shares began trading on the official bourse on Monday, adding some $2 billion to the BSE's capitalisation which was calculated at less than $400 million before the move.
The shares began the week on high notes with B shares closing at $120 on Tuesday and A shares reaching $115.125 a day earlier.
"This initial rise (in the shares' prices) was expected immediately after the move to the official market," a dealer said.
Weekly turnover on the BSE was 21,291 shares from 25,140 last week and value was $2,444,065 from $2,828,651.
Also traded during the week were 4,000 Ciments Libanais shares at $1.3125, unchanged from September 20.
There was no trade in any of the other three listed companies throughout the week: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
The Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) rose 0.32 percent on the week to 84.01 and the BLOM Stock Index (BSI) rose 0.19 to 966.1.
